title: burgee --schema
description: The document `<program> --schema` prints: the program as data, for an agent or an MCP host to read without running anything. Published so a reader can validate what a program says about itself (burgee F1, D-123); burgee's own test validates `--schema` output against this file on every run.

schemaVersion.description: Bumped only when a field changes meaning.

clispec.description: The version of The CLI Spec (https://clispec.dev) the document also conforms to. A native program's `--schema` carries it, and every key clispec defines beside burgee's own; a commander- or yargs-syntax program's, and the summary over budget, do not.

exitCodes.description: What each exit code means (F1): the contract's names and numbers, so a caller branches on the code without reading prose.

explain.description: How to ask where an option's value came from: `--explain <option>` on a command. A native program's `--schema` carries it ahead of `commands`; a commander- or yargs-syntax program's does not (D-20261009-b1-totals-and-explain).

global_args.description: The flags every command takes, exactly as root help lists them under `Global options:` (clispec v0.3 `global_args`).

output.description: What a run prints when no format is asked for (clispec v0.3 `output`): text at a terminal and under a pipe; `--json` and `--format` select the others.

errors.description: Every kind of failure the program can leave with, and its exit code (clispec v0.3 `errors`): the contract's kinds, then each class the program defined with `defineError`. A failure's envelope names its kind in `error.kind`. A native program's `--schema` carries it; a commander- or yargs-syntax program's does not.

commands.description: Every runnable, visible command, in declaration order.

shadows.description: The reserved surfaces a commander- or yargs-syntax program declares for itself, which burgee therefore withholds (J4): the program wins, and the document says so. Absent when it shadows none; a native program cannot shadow them (V5).

kind.description: The word the failure is, in snake_case: `usage`, `auth`, `timeout`, or a defined error's own.

exit_code.description: The exit code it leaves with.

retryable.description: Whether running the same command again may succeed.

name.description: The command as typed, without the program name: `config get`.

aliases.description: Other words that run the command (R5); never a command of their own.

default.description: It runs when argv names no command at its parent's level (default-command R4); at most one per level.

effects.description: What running it does to the world, or `withheld` (N6).

fields.description: The result's top-level fields, what `--json=` selects from (N14).

relations.description: Constraints between options (S2, S6): exactlyOneOf, atLeastOneOf, atMostOneOf, conflicts, implies.

example.description: The first of `examples` as the arguments to run it with, without the program's name (clispec v0.3 `example`). Native programs only.

output_kind.description: `output.kind` as declared (clispec v0.3). Native programs only.

media_type.description: `output.mediaType` of an opaque command (clispec v0.3). Native programs only.

cardinality.description: `output.cardinality` as declared: how many results come back (clispec v0.3). Native programs only.

stdout_schema.description: What `--json` prints on success: the envelope, with `output.schema` (or an object of the declared `fields`) as its `data` (clispec v0.3). Native programs only.

type.description: What the word is, as the handler reads it (typed-positionals R1); absent is `string`. `file`: `-` means standard input (S4).

default.description: A string, boolean, number, or a list of strings or numbers.

schema.description: A Standard Schema validator, as its own library serialises it.

negatable.description: Booleans only: whether `--no-<name>` is accepted. Absent means yes; a commander-syntax program's option says `false` where commander would refuse the negation (D-134).

inputSchema.description: The arguments and options as one JSON Schema object — what an MCP tool call takes.
